subject: general
question: On what date were the Consumer Protection (Direct Selling) Rules, 2021 introduced by the Government of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dec 28 2021 **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dec 28 2021** is the date on which the Consumer Protection (Direct Selling) Rules, 2021 were introduced by the Government of India.
 
• These rules are part of the Consumer Protection Act, which aims to protect the interests of consumers in India.
 
• The rules provide a regulatory framework for direct selling and aim to prevent unfair trade practices.
 
• They also ensure that direct sellers and direct selling entities comply with certain obligations to safeguard consumer interests.
 
• The introduction of these rules marks a significant step in enhancing consumer rights and promoting fair trade practices in the direct selling industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Consumer Protection Act, 2019** was enacted to replace the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, and it came into force on 20th July 2020.
 
• The Act provides for the establishment of the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) to promote, protect, and enforce the rights of consumers.
 
• The Act includes provisions for the prevention of unfair trade practices, product liability, and the establishment of consumer dispute redressal commissions.
 
• The **Consumer Protection (Direct Selling) Rules, 2021** are part of the comprehensive legal framework aimed at strengthening consumer protection in India.
 
• Direct selling entities must adhere to these rules to operate legally in India, ensuring transparency and accountability in their business practices.
 
• The rules also mandate that direct sellers provide accurate information about the products and services they offer, thereby protecting consumers from misleading claims.
